sources.entry: Super Productivity - Free to do list & time tracker for programmers & designers with Jira integration.

summary.one_liner: Super Productivity is an open-source, offline-first to-do list, time tracker and daily planner that can also integrate with many issue trackers.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a task manager for focused personal work with sub-tasks, projects, tags and color coding. It includes a daily planner with a schedule timeline alongside calendar events, and visual boards such as Kanban and Eisenhower Matrix. Time tracking covers timeboxing, time sheets and work summaries for export, plus a focus mode with Pomodoro, Flowtime and countdown sessions and a break reminder. It can import tasks from Jira, Trello, GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, OpenProject, Linear, ClickUp, Redmine, Nextcloud Deck and Azure DevOps, and offers basic CalDAV integration. Data sync is offered through SuperSync, Dropbox and WebDAV, and the README says it collects no data and needs no account.
use_cases: track time spent on tasks for timesheets
plan my day with a timeline and calendar
manage tasks imported from Jira or GitHub
organize tasks on a Kanban or Eisenhower board
sync to-do data across devices privately
how_to_run: Open the web app at the project's hosted site, or download a desktop/mobile build from the wiki
See the wiki's Downloads & Install page for platform-specific package links and notes
For development: follow the wiki's 'Run dev server' guide
To self-host sync: see the wiki's Sync Server documentation
stack: Electron-style desktop packaging (inferred from 'package the app' docs; not explicitly named)
notable: Offline-first with no account or registration; user chooses where data is stored
Built-in Kanban and Eisenhower Matrix boards
Integrations with about ten issue trackers, including Jira, GitHub, Linear and Azure DevOps
SuperSync is end-to-end encrypted and can be self-hosted
caveats: The web version has limitations compared with the desktop app (see the README's comparison link)
